title: tasq 3.0.0 npm release
context: tasq is an open-source (MIT) task-runner CLI with about 180k weekly npm downloads. Its docs recommend running `tasq lint-staged` in git pre-commit hooks and `tasq run` in CI and editor integrations. This proposal publishes 3.0.0 to npm and announces it on the project blog.
artifact:
# Release proposal: tasq 3.0.0 (npm)

Maintainers: core team · Publish: Thu 2026-11-12 · Tracking: #1840 · Blog: "tasq 3: plugins for everyone"

## Highlights

- **Zero-config plugins.** Any installed package with the `tasq-plugin` keyword is picked up automatically. No more `plugins: [...]` array in `tasq.config.ts`.
- **Task graph caching** keyed on input file hashes; repeated `tasq run build` with unchanged inputs completes in under 50 ms of task time.
- **ESM-only**, Node 20+.

## Breaking changes

| Change | Migration |
|---|---|
| Node 18 support dropped | Node 18 is EOL since April 2025; `engines` field enforces `>=20` |
| CommonJS `require('tasq')` removed | `npx tasq-migrate` rewrites config files and `require` calls; tested on 40 public repos, 38 fully automatic, 2 needed manual edits (documented) |
| `plugins` array in config ignored | Auto-discovery replaces it; `tasq-migrate` removes the array and installs nothing new |
| `tasq lint-staged` output format | JSON reporter unchanged; pretty reporter shows grouped output |

## How plugin discovery works

On every invocation (`tasq run`, `tasq lint-staged`, `tasq watch` restarts, `tasq list`), the CLI walks `node_modules` (including nested `node_modules` in workspaces), reads each `package.json`, and loads the ones whose `keywords` include `tasq-plugin`. Discovery runs before argument parsing so that plugins can register subcommands.

```ts
// src/plugins/discover.ts
export async function discoverPlugins(root: string): Promise<PluginRef[]> {
  const found: PluginRef[] = [];
  for await (const pkgJson of glob("**/node_modules/**/package.json", { cwd: root })) {
    const pkg = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(root, pkgJson), "utf8"));
    if (pkg.keywords?.includes("tasq-plugin")) found.push({ name: pkg.name, dir: dirname(pkgJson) });
  }
  return found;
}
```

## Performance (reference monorepo: 61 workspaces, 2,430 installed packages, M2 MacBook Air, warm disk cache)

| Command | 2.9.4 | 3.0.0-rc.2 |
|---|---|---|
| `tasq --version` | 0.11 s | 1.94 s |
| `tasq lint-staged` (3 staged files) | 0.38 s | 2.31 s |
| `tasq run build` (cache hit) | 0.21 s | 2.02 s |
| `tasq run build` (cold, full build) | 48.7 s | 46.1 s |

Discovery is a fixed per-invocation cost and becomes negligible relative to real build work, so overall build time improves thanks to the new graph cache.

## Supply chain and licensing

- Published from GitHub Actions with npm provenance (`--provenance`); 2FA required for all maintainers.
- No `postinstall` scripts in tasq or its dependencies.
- New runtime deps: `fast-glob` (MIT), `semver` (ISC). License scan: no copyleft dependencies.

## QA summary

- Unit + integration: 1,912 tests pass on Linux/macOS/Windows, Node 20 and 22.
- `tasq-migrate` on 40 public repos (list in #1840): 38 automatic, 2 manual (Yarn PnP projects, documented).
- Smoke test of top 15 community plugins under auto-discovery: all load and register subcommands.

## Release and support plan

1. Publish `3.0.0` under `next` dist-tag; promote to `latest` after 7 days with no P1 issues.
2. `2.x` moves to `latest-2` dist-tag and receives security fixes until 2027-11-12. Announced in the README and blog post.
3. Rollback: if a P1 is found after promotion, re-point `latest` to `2.9.4` (`npm dist-tag add tasq@2.9.4 latest`) and publish a fix as 3.0.1.
4. Blog post and changelog go live at publish; Discord announcement links the migration guide.

defects.description: Plugin auto-discovery globs every package.json under node_modules on every invocation, before argument parsing. Per the proposal's own benchmark, that adds about 1.8-2s to every command, even `tasq --version` and cache hits. Every git commit (lint-staged hook) and every editor/CI call gets 6-17x slower, and the 'negligible relative to build work' argument ignores the documented hot paths. Discovery needs caching (e.g. keyed on lockfile hash) or lazy loading before release.

decoys: Dropping Node 18 and CommonJS is a breaking change, but it ships in a major version with an `engines` field, a codemod tested on 40 repos, and 12 months of 2.x security fixes on the latest-2 dist-tag.

Auto-loading arbitrary installed packages may look like a supply-chain risk, but those packages are already installed and executable in the project. The release itself uses npm provenance, mandatory 2FA, no postinstall scripts and a license scan with no copyleft dependencies.
